text:
maya: kicking off a short thread to align on the isolation graduation plan — we need a concrete launch checklist + migration waves for tenants
kevin: awesome — can we keep it as waves based on risk + traffic size? small low-risk customers first, then medium, then high. also need routing policy DSL to enable soft-fallbacks
sophie: agree on waves. infra needs clear SLA and eviction budget per wave otherwise we can't reserve capacity. propose: Wave 0 (internal), Wave 1 (<5% customers, no region pins), Wave 2 (10-20%, region-aware), Wave 3 (high revenue, cust-specific contracts) :warning:
aj: from product ops: add acceptance criteria — performance regressions <=5% p95 latency, cost delta <=10% per token, no customer-facing errors >1 per 24h during pilot :ok_hand:
liam: must include observability hooks: token-level cost traces, per-tenant KV cache hit rates, and a fast rollback path. also need canary traffic splitter with manual kill switch
kevin: for the routing policy DSL draft (very rough):
```
policy "isolation-tier" {
  priority: [ "region-affinity", "tenant-quota", "cost-tier" ]
  fallback: [ "quantized-small", "regional-pool", "shared-host" ]
  eviction_score_threshold: 0.8
}
```
kevin: this lets ops pick fallback combos per wave
sophie: infra note — regional-pool fallback requires cross-region bandwidth budget. we need a cross-region egress cap per tenant in Wave 2+, and an emergency throttle for wave 3
maya: launch criteria brainstorm (putting together bullet list):
- Successful internal canary for 72h with no regressions
- Wave 1: 7-day pilot with 5 customers, p95 latency change <5%
- Telemetry dashboards validated by SRE + PM
- Rollout runbook and rollback <10 minutes
- Legal/security sign-off for Wave 3 customers
aj: also include opt-in contract terms for paid customers: migration window, data residency opt-out, credit for migration disruption :money_with_wings:
liam: operational acceptance tests to add to runbook:
- simulated node evacuation (chaos)
- KV cache warm-up verification
- cold-start tail-latency under target
kevin: question for product: do we want to gate waves on model-variant parity? i.e., ensure fallback models produce >=X BLEU/ROUGE or acceptance evals
maya: yes, quality parity gate. propose eval-suite pass rate >=95% on our golden prompts for any fallback config used in a wave
sophie: cost modeling: we should produce cost delta per tenant projection for each wave — we can automate with a small script but need sample prompts from customers
aj: ops will reach out to pilot tenants to gather samples this week
infra-bot: reminder — new RFC template available at https://internal.redwood/rfc/isolation-grade. Use tag `isolation-wave`
maya: next steps: Kevin + Sophie to draft the routing DSL + cost model by EOD Thu, Liam to draft acceptance tests, AJ to line up pilot tenants. I'll collect into a one-pager for exec sync Friday. thanks everyone :pray:
